problem.text: The interactive chat loop streamed replies without reporting prompt-processing throughput, cache reuse or generation throughput.

reasoning.text: The change reuses the generator's completion metadata rather than introducing chat-side timers. It separates uncached prompt work from cached tokens and generated tokens.

impact.text: -tps/--show_tps enables a statistics line after replies; the new /tps command mistakenly toggles multiline input instead. The displayed Context token count also mistakenly repeats the generated-token count.

source_notes.text: Read the initial usage-evaluation entry and the interactive-controls entry. They establish the earlier conversation-generation pipeline and local command-state design; the latter also records an unchecked code-block index.
The recorded code-block index problem is carried over: the parent helper indexes matches[-num] without a lower bound, main forwards negative integers, and neither task section changes that path.

Closed discussions retain distinct framing: #6, “No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr'”, concerns startup; #12, “Qwen2.5 Coder 0.5B Instruct | ValueError: Unsupported type in stop_conditions”, concerns prompt mode; #39, “Gemma 3 architecture not in list?”, concerns branch availability and frontend behavior; #43, “Error converting abliterated Qwen3 mlabonne/Qwen3-30B-A3B-abliterated”, concerns conversion; and PR #22, “OpenAI compatible API example”, proposes an endpoint. Their connection to this task is inferred only from references to chat.py, not evidence that they motivated statistics.

limitations: No model generation or interactive terminal session was executed. The Python check transcribed state changes, statistics arithmetic and indexing only.
The new throughput divisions have no zero-duration guard. Actual timer resolution and occurrence of zero durations were not established.
Whole-parent-tree literal caller searches establish the script entry point, not compatibility with external or dynamically resolved callers.

claims.text: The parser adds a store_true -tps/--show_tps option, so reporting is opt-in. main snapshots args.show_tps and prints after streaming finishes and after any response-length warning, before storing the reply in conversation history.

The statistics use the trimmed, formatted input's ids.shape[-1]. Subtracting cached_tokens gives the numerator for prompt throughput; generation throughput uses r['new_tokens']. Job's EOS result supplies these counts and durations: time_prefill spans first prefill to first token, while time_generate spans first token to completion. These are application timing intervals, not isolated kernel benchmarks.

The existing dynamic_gen statistics consumer gates access on streaming EOS results and adds 1e-10 seconds to throughput denominators. Chat instead reads the final loop result after its single job drains and divides directly. Its .3f formatting selects three decimal places, not a measurement-accuracy guarantee.

The command follows the existing command-before-generation structure and continues without creating a model turn. However, its assignment and status-message condition use multiline, whereas the reporting gate uses show_tps. Both console-output modes pass multiline to read_input_ptk, which forwards it to prompt_toolkit.

A standard-library transcription with 100 prompt tokens, 40 cached tokens, a two-second prefill and ten generated tokens in half a second produced “Context: 10 new tokens at 30.000 t/s”, although uncached context work was 60 tokens. It also preserved show_tps across /tps for both initial boolean values while changing multiline.
The console edit changes only the col_info comment from “Bright red” to “Green”; the ANSI value remains unchanged. It supplies no runtime prerequisite for statistics.

Whole-tree searches found no existing show_tps occurrence or chat-module import caller. The script's own parser-to-main call supplies the newly accessed attribute; external Namespace builders were not established.

findings.description: /tps changes input mode rather than statistics visibility.
findings.trigger: Enter /tps in an active chat session.
findings.expected_behavior: Toggle tokens-per-second reporting without changing multiline input.
findings.actual_behavior: multiline flips, its value controls the confirmation message, and show_tps remains unchanged. This reaches both basic and rich output modes through main's shared command branch.

verification.description: Transcribed the assignment for both initial show_tps values; reporting state stayed fixed while multiline became true.

findings.description: The Context count reports generated tokens rather than uncached prompt tokens.
findings.trigger: Enable --show_tps and complete a reply whose generated-token count differs from prompt_tokens minus cached_tokens.
findings.expected_behavior: Display the uncached prompt count alongside the prompt throughput computed from that count.
findings.actual_behavior: new_tokens is overwritten with r['new_tokens'] before formatting both Context and Generate, pairing the generated count with prompt throughput. The script entry point reaches this shared post-stream block in either output mode.

verification.description: For 60 uncached prompt tokens and ten generated tokens, the transcribed output displayed Context: 10 while retaining 60/2 = 30 t/s.
verification.limits: Synthetic metadata; no inference or timing measurement.

findings.description: The previously recorded unchecked negative code-block index persists unchanged.
findings.trigger: Enter /cc -2 after a response containing exactly two matched fenced code blocks.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject or normalize the invalid block number without terminating chat.
findings.actual_behavior: The helper indexes matches[2] and raises IndexError before copying. main catches integer parsing failures only. Whole-tree search found its /cc branch as the sole literal helper caller.

verification.description: Transcribed fenced-block matching and negative indexing with two blocks; observed IndexError.
verification.limits: Did not execute the helper, clipboard backend or chat session.

annotation.summary: Adds opt-in chat throughput statistics and a /tps command, but the command toggles multiline input and the Context count repeats generated tokens. The console change is comment-only.
